# gmti-segment

One STANAG 4607 segment (AEDP-4607 Edition A Version 1): the 5-byte segment header and its body,
with the same kinds, keys and lines as `gmti` and no packet header. `distribution public`.

Layouts from NATO standardization documents published on the NSG Standards Registry; NATO is
acknowledged as their source. They are restated in this project's own words; see PROVENANCE.md.

A packet holds any number of segments, one after another, each starting with its type and its
size (the 5 header bytes included). The pack language cannot read a list that runs to the end of
the packet with no count (see `gmti`), so a caller splits the packet: skip the 32-byte packet
header (decode it with `gmti`, which reads the first segment as well), then cut segment after
segment at its size and decode each with `gmti-segment`. The vectors `split-*` show a packet of
three segments cut this way.

The packet header's platform, mission and job are not in a segment. The derived `uid` of a dwell
needs them: supply them as context (`--set gmti.platform_id=... --set gmti.mission_id=... --set
gmti.job_id=...`). Without them a dwell has no `uid`.

| kind | segment type | fields | bound to shared keys |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mission` | 1 | 7 | 0 |
| `dwell` | 2 | 48 | 3 |
| `hrr` | 3 | 30 | 0 |
| `jobdef` | 5 | 28 | 0 |
| `freetext` | 6 | 2 | 0 |
| `teststatus` | 10 | 6 | 0 |
| `prochist` | 12 | 11 | 0 |
| `location` | 13 | 7 | 6 |
| `jobreq` | 101 | 26 | 0 |
| `joback` | 102 | 25 | 0 |

194 `field` and `also` lines. What the segment kinds do not read is listed in `gmti/pack.md`;
the repeated records of a dwell, an HRR segment and a processing history segment are read by
`gmti-segment-records`.

## Message convention

Hex text of one segment, most significant bit first. Input after the stated segment size is
ignored. Vectors are synthetic, packed by `tools/gmti/vectors.py`.
